Load required packages

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(data.table)
  library(rprojroot)
  library(R.utils)
  library(ggsci)
  library(ggforce)
  library(ggpubr)
})
```

Set directory paths

```{r}
root_dir <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_dir(".git"))
data_dir <- file.path(root_dir, "data")
analysis_dir <- file.path(root_dir, "analyses", "05-summarize-TEJs")
input_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "input")
results_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "results")
plot_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "plots")
if (!dir.exists(results_dir)) {
  dir.create(results_dir)
}

source(file.path(root_dir, "figures", "theme_for_plots.R"))
source(file.path(analysis_dir, "util", "annotation_functions.R"))
```

Set file paths

```{r}
tej_file <- file.path(results_dir,
                       "recurrent-primary-tumor-enriched-oncofetal-splice-junctions.tsv.gz")

gtf_file <- file.path(data_dir,
                      "gencode.v39.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz")

splice_event_file <- file.path(root_dir, "analyses",
                               "04-tej-differential-splicing",
                               "results",
                               "tumor-enriched-oncofetal-junction-diff-splice-event-annotation.tsv.gz")
```

Wrangle data

```{r}
tej_df <- read_tsv(tej_file)

gtf <- rtracklayer::import(gtf_file)

# rtracklayer keeps only the last value of repeated GTF attributes, so the
# imported `tag` column usually misses "MANE_Select". Read MANE Select
# transcript IDs directly from the GTF text instead.
mane_tx_ids <- readr::read_lines_chunked(
  gtf_file,
  readr::ListCallback$new(function(x, pos) {
    x <- x[grepl('tag "MANE_Select"', x, fixed = TRUE)]
    stringr::str_match(x, 'transcript_id "([^"]+)"')[, 2]
  }),
  chunk_size = 1e5
) %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unique()

gtf_df <- as.data.frame(gtf) %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "exon") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(is_mane = transcript_id %in% mane_tx_ids)
```

Determine if TEJ exons map to GTF-annotated exons

```{r}
starts <- gtf_df %>%
  distinct(seqnames, start, end, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(chr_start = glue::glue("{seqnames}:{start}")) %>%
  pull(chr_start)

ends <- gtf_df %>%
  distinct(seqnames, start, end, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(chr_start = glue::glue("{seqnames}:{end}")) %>%
  pull(chr_start)

# GENCODE introns ("{chr}:{exon end}-{next exon start}") from consecutive
# exons of every transcript
gencode_introns <- gtf_df %>%
  dplyr::select(seqnames, transcript_id, start, end) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(transcript_id, start) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(transcript_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(next_start = dplyr::lead(start)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(next_start)) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(intron = glue::glue("{seqnames}:{end}-{next_start}")) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  pull(intron)

tej_annot_df <- tej_df %>%
  # retain unique TEJs
  distinct(junction, gene_symbol, preference_code, chr,
           up_jc_start, up_jc_end, down_jc_start, down_jc_end,
           strand) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(chr = case_when(
    grepl("KI", chr) ~ str_remove(chr, "chr"),
    TRUE ~ chr
  )) %>%
  # define exon coords for GTF mapping
  dplyr::mutate(up_bound = glue::glue("{chr}:{up_jc_end}"),
                down_bound = glue::glue("{chr}:{down_jc_start}")) %>%
  # determine if junction bounds are annotated
  dplyr::mutate(up_bound_annotated = case_when(
    up_bound %in% ends ~ "Yes",
    TRUE ~ "No"
  )) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(down_bound_annotated = case_when(
    down_bound %in% starts ~ "Yes",
    TRUE ~ "No"
  )) %>%
  # determine if the junction itself is a GENCODE intron
  dplyr::mutate(junction_in_gencode = glue::glue("{chr}:{up_jc_end}-{down_jc_start}") %in% gencode_introns)

# if exon-exon boundary and one boundary not annotated, classify as novel
tej_annot_df <- tej_annot_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(novel_ss = case_when(
    preference_code == "RI" & up_bound_annotated == "No" & down_bound_annotated == "No" ~ "Yes",
    preference_code == "RI" ~ "No",
    up_bound_annotated == "No" | down_bound_annotated == "No" ~ "Yes",
    TRUE ~ "No"
  ))
```

Obtain the skipped (cassette) exon of each ES junction and the retained intron of each RI junction from the junction's consensus rMATS event

```{r}
# Select the consensus splice event per junction as in
# 06-generate-tej-psi-matrix.Rmd: the most frequent splice_id among samples
# whose event type matches the junction's consensus event type.
consensus_event_df <- read_tsv(splice_event_file) %>%
  dplyr::filter(junction %in% tej_annot_df$junction,
                consensus_jc_event_type %in% c("exon skipping", "intron retention"),
                event_type_sample == consensus_jc_event_type) %>%
  dplyr::count(junction, splice_id, consensus_jc_event_type) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  distinct(junction, .keep_all = TRUE)

# SE splice_ids are
# "{chr}:{exonStart}-{exonEnd}_{upstreamES}-{upstreamEE}_{downstreamES}-{downstreamEE}_{strand}"
# with 1-based starts, so the first interval is the skipped exon.
skipped_exon_df <- consensus_event_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(consensus_jc_event_type == "exon skipping") %>%
  tidyr::extract(splice_id,
                 into = c("skipped_exon_start", "skipped_exon_end"),
                 regex = "^[^:]+:(\\d+)-(\\d+)_",
                 convert = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::select(junction, skipped_exon_start, skipped_exon_end)

# RI splice_ids are
# "{chr}:{riExonStart_0base}-{riExonEnd}_{upstreamES}-{upstreamEE}_{downstreamES}-{downstreamEE}_{strand}"
# with 1-based upstreamES/downstreamES; the retained intron lies between
# upstreamEE and downstreamES.
retained_intron_df <- consensus_event_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(consensus_jc_event_type == "intron retention") %>%
  tidyr::extract(splice_id,
                 into = c("ri_upstream_exon_end", "ri_downstream_exon_start"),
                 regex = "^[^:]+:\\d+-\\d+_\\d+-(\\d+)_(\\d+)-\\d+_",
                 convert = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::select(junction, ri_upstream_exon_end, ri_downstream_exon_start)

tej_annot_df <- tej_annot_df %>%
  left_join(skipped_exon_df, by = "junction") %>%
  left_join(retained_intron_df, by = "junction")

# RI TEJs are exon-intron boundaries, so they never match a GENCODE intron.
# Treat an RI TEJ as annotated when a GENCODE exon (any transcript type)
# spans its retained intron.
gtf_exon_dt <- gtf_df %>%
  dplyr::transmute(seqnames = as.character(seqnames), start, end) %>%
  data.table::as.data.table()

ri_query_dt <- tej_annot_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ri_upstream_exon_end)) %>%
  distinct(junction, chr, ri_upstream_exon_end, ri_downstream_exon_start) %>%
  data.table::as.data.table()

ri_annotated_jcs <- gtf_exon_dt[
  ri_query_dt,
  on = .(seqnames = chr,
         start <= ri_upstream_exon_end,
         end >= ri_downstream_exon_start),
  nomatch = 0L,
  unique(i.junction)
]

tej_annot_df <- tej_annot_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(junction_in_gencode = case_when(
    preference_code == "RI" ~ junction %in% ri_annotated_jcs,
    TRUE ~ junction_in_gencode
  ))
```

Run `annotate_junctions()` function to annotate junctions to transcripts, exons, and introns.

A GTF exon matches a junction when its junction-facing splice site matches; the distal exon boundary is not compared.
For exon skipping (ES) TEJs, the skipped exon comes from the junction's consensus rMATS SE event (chunk above).

When several transcripts contain both junction-facing exons, they are ranked by:

1. ES only: contains the rMATS skipped exon
2. ES only: skips at least one exon between the two junction-facing exons
3. junction-facing exons adjacent in the transcript (for non-ES events, a non-adjacent label would imply an additional exon skip)
4. protein-coding
5. MANE Select (GTF `tag "MANE_Select"`)
6. transcript support level (1 best; NA last)
7. transcript name

When only one junction-facing exon is annotated (novel donor/acceptor, RI), or the two exons share no transcript, each exon's transcript is ranked by protein-coding, MANE Select, TSL, then name.

`cassette_status` (ES TEJs only; `NA` otherwise) records where the rMATS skipped exon (matched on both boundaries, within the gene) is annotated:

* `in chosen transcript`: the labelled transcript contains it
* `annotated elsewhere`: another transcript of the gene contains it
* `novel`: no transcript of the gene contains it

Labels list the genomically upstream (lower coordinate) side first, so minus-strand labels read against the direction of transcription: for a minus-strand gene, `exon4:exon2` is a junction from exon 2 to exon 4.

`status` does not depend on the chosen transcript: `Novel splice site` when a junction-facing splice site is unannotated, `Annotated junction` when the junction is an intron of any GENCODE transcript, otherwise `Novel junction`.
RI TEJs are exon-intron boundaries rather than exon-exon junctions, so for them `Annotated junction` means a GENCODE exon of any transcript type spans the retained intron of the junction's consensus rMATS RI event.

```{r}
# Subset gtf to make for easier filtering within function. Keep exons at
# junction-facing boundaries and candidate rMATS skipped exons.
gtf_sub_dt <- gtf_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(start %in% tej_annot_df$down_jc_start |
                  end %in% tej_annot_df$up_jc_end |
                  start %in% tej_annot_df$skipped_exon_start) %>%
  data.table::as.data.table()

# Create the splice-boundary lookup indices once. These are reused for every
# junction annotation instead of sorting/copying the GTF within each function call.
data.table::setindexv(gtf_sub_dt, c("seqnames", "gene_name", "end"))
data.table::setindexv(gtf_sub_dt, c("seqnames", "gene_name", "start"))

# run annotation
system.time({
  tej_annot_df <- tej_annot_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      annot = suppressMessages(pmap(
          pick(chr,
               up_jc_start,
               up_jc_end,
               down_jc_start,
               down_jc_end,
               gene_symbol,
               preference_code,
               skipped_exon_start,
               skipped_exon_end),
          \(...) annotate_junctions(
            chr = ..1,
            up_exon_start = ..2,
            up_exon_end = ..3,
            down_exon_start = ..4,
            down_exon_end = ..5,
            gene_symbol = ..6,
            preference = ..7,
            gtf = gtf_sub_dt,
            skipped_exon_start = ..8,
            skipped_exon_end = ..9
          )
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    # split annotation into junction_name, transcript_id, and
    # cassette_status columns
    tidyr::unnest_wider(annot)
})
```

Join annotation to recurrent TEJ data frame

```{r}
tej_df <- tej_df %>%
  left_join(tej_annot_df %>%
              distinct(junction,
                      novel_ss,
                      junction_name,
                      transcript_id,
                      cassette_status,
                      junction_in_gencode)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    up_exon = case_when(
      grepl(":exon", junction_name) ~ sapply(
        strsplit(junction_name, ", |:"),
        function(x) if (length(x) >= 2) x[2] else NA_character_
      ),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    down_exon = case_when(
      grepl(":exon", junction_name) ~ sapply(
        strsplit(junction_name, ", |:"),
        function(x) if (length(x) >= 2) x[3] else NA_character_
      ),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(up_exon = as.numeric(str_remove(up_exon, "exon")),
                down_exon = as.numeric(str_remove(down_exon, "exon"))) %>%
  # Annotated junction: the junction is an intron of any GENCODE transcript
  # (RI: a GENCODE exon spans the retained intron), independent of the
  # transcript chosen for junction_name
  dplyr::mutate(status = case_when(
    grepl("novel", junction_name) ~ "Novel splice site",
    junction_in_gencode ~ "Annotated junction",
    TRUE ~ "Novel junction"
  )) %>%
  dplyr::select(-junction_in_gencode)
```

Plot novel splice site usage frequency among tejs by histology

```{r}
unique_hist_tej_ct <- tej_df %>%
  distinct(plot_group, junction) %>%
  dplyr::count(plot_group) %>%
  dplyr::rename(hist_tej_n = n)

hist_tej_novelss_ct <- tej_df %>%
  distinct(junction, plot_group, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::count(plot_group, status) %>%
  left_join(unique_hist_tej_ct) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(n_norm = n/hist_tej_n)

hist_order <- c("Other CNS embryonal tumor", 
                "Pineoblastoma", "Oligodendroglioma",
                "Neurofibroma plexiform", "Mesenchymal tumor", 
                "Rare CNS tumor", "Germ cell tumor",
                "Meningioma", "Schwannoma/MPNST", 
                "Non-neoplastic tumor", "Craniopharyngioma", 
                "Mixed neuronal-glial tumor",
                "Atypical Teratoid Rhabdoid Tumor", 
                "Choroid plexus tumor", "Ependymoma",
                "DIPG or DMG", "Other high-grade glioma",
                "Low-grade glioma", "Medulloblastoma")

# generate plot
novelss_freq_barplot <- hist_tej_novelss_ct %>%
  dplyr::filter(status != "Annotated junction") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(plot_group = fct_relevel(plot_group,
                                        as.character(hist_order))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(y = plot_group, x = n_norm, fill = status)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", show.legend = TRUE) + 
  scale_fill_npg() +
  theme_Publication() +
  labs(x = "Proportion TEJs",
     y = NULL,
     fill = "Junction annotation")

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir,
                 "tejs-by-junction-status-hist-barplot.pdf"),
       novelss_freq_barplot,
       width = 8, height = 6)
```
